evidence: 0088 (item 3, owner decisions D1-D19 of 2026-10-26) lets the receiving laboratory or pharmacy end a cross-facility order it accepted for someone who was not the order's patient. ehr.report_wrong_patient_order_route, through lab.report_wrong_patient_order_route and pharmacy.report_wrong_patient_order_route, is bound to the live direct-care staff session and the kind's receive permission; in one transaction it invalidates every result recorded on the order (each version that came back to the ordering facility is reported there as entered in error) or reverses its dispensing, ends the route through 0086's closer (accepted -> cancelled, completed -> access ended, ended_kind 'wrong_patient', both windows now), writes the report row support reviews (ehr.order_route_wrong_patient_reports), a system audit row at each facility and the patient's inbox notice ORDER_ROUTE_WRONG_PATIENT. Withdrawing needs lab.result.entered-in-error or pharmacy.dispensing.reverse; the state is checked before the version, so an order ended any other way answers ORDER_ROUTE_ALREADY_ENDED; a key reused with another request answers IDEMPOTENCY_KEY_REUSED, also when that request is a report on another route that committed after both lookups (the key's unique index, caught, never 23505). Support lists the reports and reviews each once (identity.admin_list_wrong_patient_reports with platform.facility.read, identity.admin_review_wrong_patient_report with platform.facility.manage); the reporter's note reaches support only and may be removed once at review. The ordering facility's Overview read ehr.list_sent_wrong_patient_order_routes (D10's alternative (a)) gives full rows only for orders the member sent and whose patient's record they may still read, a count and references for the facility's others, nothing without ehr.order-route.send. Preconditions pin the two replaced bodies (ehr.order_route_item_access md5 53ca1585b8af43ee1340d980829fac79: a write on such a route is closed even under the patient's consent; lab.return_order_route_result md5 d0edd43f960cb75a87055c9f298247b0: a release on such a route is refused), the three dropped and recreated route cards (md5 34bf018487660e12900df69f6ff1fb14, 279297469487e3f0cf8b3360c30c5bce, 2a74a6f9ef676fd03d7ee337027acf8b; two trailing columns, row_version and ended_kind, given back to their recorded owner with 0086's security, volatility and search path, then checked), 23 relied-upon bodies, the two ended-kind and two event CHECKs (compared with the same CHECKs built in the session), the route's two triggers and the four return triggers. Locks: before section 6 only momentary ACCESS SHARE on ehr.order_routes, ehr.order_route_events and lab.result_revisions (pg_get_constraintdef and the PL/pgSQL validator), each released at once (measured with pg_locks at every section boundary; with ACCESS EXCLUSIVE held on one of those three tables the runner's lock_timeout stops the apply with nothing applied); section 6 takes ACCESS EXCLUSIVE on ehr.order_routes NOWAIT, 50 attempts over 5 seconds, then 55P03 with nothing applied (measured with a reader holding ACCESS SHARE, in the dry run and in the apply), and holds it for 28-39 ms on a small copy and about 100 ms with 100,000 routes, in each of the dry run and the apply. 0088 never locks platform.control_settings or identity.consent_grants. Old images on the new schema: 595c044's Lab and Pharmacy card queries name their 13 columns and read the recreated cards unchanged, and their accept, decline, list and get calls answer as before (run on a 0088 copy); the replaced bodies change only routes ended 'wrong_patient', which only the new services create. Grants: the Lab and Pharmacy commands and cards to their runtimes, support's two to hid_identity_runtime, the Overview read to hid_ehr_runtime, all but support's also to hid_schema_test_runtime, in the migration and in runtime-grants.sql. Suites: services/ehr-api/test/database/order-routes-wrong-patient.integration.sql and order-routes-wrong-patient-overview.integration.sql, with the order-routes privileges, lifecycle, patient, returns and concurrency suites extended. The website release, dormant until this backend, ships before this release (D15).
